title: Sidney Bechet's offer to join him in Boston, turned down for his sick mother
summary: Bechet heard Morand playing with Walter Nelson at the Silver Store and sent a telegram offering a Boston job. Morand declined to stay with his sick mother, working the Gulf Coast during the war, and now regrets it.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Around that time, didn't you get an offer from Sidney Boucher to join him in Boston? A few years after that, at least.

Yeah, when Sidney came down here to play the jazz concert at the auditorium with Lewis Armstrong, he had a chance to hear me. He had a chance to hear me. At that time, I was playing with Walter Nelson. He is standing right behind me at the Silver Store at St. Bernard and in that street, I think, or 8 Court. And we was playing there with Walter Nelson, one of the greatest blues guitar players in New Orleans. I am playing with him right now at this time right now. He's standing right over me. Just happened to come in. And we was playing at the Silver Store and Sidney came in. And that's where Sidney had a chance to hear me. So he sat down and he asked me to play different numbers for him. And we played it for him. So he went back to New York, I think. So he got an opportunity to use me in Boston. Sent a telegram and everything, which was a great offer. But at that time, my mother was sick and I hadn't been home for so long. And I don't think it's a job in the world. I don't care how much money it would pay. And would make me leave my mother. And I know she felt bad if I leave. And I know if I get up in Boston, New York, it would be a long time before I come back again. And the doctor gave up. So I said, well, I'm going to stay down here. I'll have to turn down all offers. But I was doing nice during the war. It's playing.

in Mississippi, Gulfport, Mississippi, Biloxi, a place like that. And I was really doing good. So, I was really sorry that I couldn't make the trip to go up there. But it's one of them things, I wouldn't leave Mama and she's sick to go for it. No, nobody. Yes, I'm sure that was
rather an unfortunate circumstance because I'm sure if you had returned to Boston,

the world would be more jazz conscious. Yeah, I would have a great opportunity to get back in New York like I wanted to. Rather conscious of the fact that you're still putting... Since jazz came back so strong, I'd have a better opportunity than before.
